task.title: Behaviour-preserving refactor of kvparse.parser
task.statement: Refactor kvparse/parser.py without changing any behaviour. Two changes are requested. (1) parse_line(line) must be rewritten without the hand-rolled index loops: split the line at the first '=' with str.partition, strip the key and the value, raise ValueError when there is no '=' or the stripped key is empty, and remove one pair of matching surrounding quotes (both ends '"' or both ends "'") from a stripped value of length two or more; the function must not contain a 'while' loop. (2) Extract the detection of ignorable lines into a module-level function _is_ignorable(line) -> bool in kvparse/parser.py that returns True exactly when the stripped line is empty or starts with '#' or ';', and make parse use it. The observable behaviour of parse and parse_line must stay byte-for-byte identical for every str input: the same return values, the same exception types in the same situations (TypeError for non-string input to parse, ValueError for a malformed line), later duplicate keys still win, and quotes are removed only when the stripped value starts and ends with the same quote character (a value like '"x\'' keeps both characters; a lone '"' is kept). Exception messages are not prescribed. parse keeps raising TypeError for non-string input; what parse_line does with a non-string argument (for example a list or a mapping) is unspecified and must not be tested, because the required use of str.partition changes it. Keep the public names parse and parse_line exported from kvparse, do not modify the tests, and keep the existing suite passing.
acceptance_criteria: parse_line raises ValueError for '', 'novalue', ' = v', '   ', '=' and '\t= 1'.

parse behaviour unchanged: comments ('#' or ';' as the first non-blank character), blank lines and Windows line endings are handled as before; later duplicate keys win; parse('') == {}; parse('k = v') == {'k': 'v'}.
parse raises ValueError for a malformed line anywhere in the text and TypeError for non-string input (None, 3, a list, bytes).

The source of parse_line contains no 'while' loop and uses str.partition.

spec.restated_task: Refactor kvparse/parser.py to replace the manual index loops in parse_line with str.partition, strip key and value, raise ValueError for missing '=' or empty key, and strip one pair of matching surrounding quotes from values of length >=2. Extract the ignorable-line detection into a module-level function _is_ignorable that returns True for empty/whitespace-only lines or lines whose first non-whitespace character is '#' or ';', and make parse use it. All observable behavior of parse and parse_line for string inputs must remain identical, including exception types and duplicate-key handling. The existing test suite must continue to pass unchanged.

interface_contract.name: parse_line
interface_contract.behavior: Splits the input line at the first '=' character using str.partition. The key is the part before '=', stripped of surrounding whitespace. The value is the part after '=', stripped of surrounding whitespace. If the stripped value has length >=2 and its first and last characters are the same quote character (either double quote '"' or single quote "'"), those surrounding quotes are removed. Returns a tuple (key, value).
error_cases: ValueError: raised when the line contains no '=' character.
ValueError: raised when the stripped key is empty.

interface_contract.name: parse
interface_contract.behavior: Splits the input text into lines using str.splitlines. For each line, if _is_ignorable(line) returns True, the line is skipped. Otherwise, parse_line(line) is called and the resulting key-value pair is added to the result dictionary; later occurrences of the same key overwrite earlier ones. Returns the dictionary.
error_cases: TypeError: raised when text is not a str.
ValueError: raised when any non-ignorable line is malformed (propagated from parse_line).

interface_contract.name: _is_ignorable
interface_contract.behavior: Returns True if the stripped line (line.strip()) is empty or its first character is '#' or ';'. Returns False otherwise. This function is module-private and only called with string arguments from parse.

limitations: Profile 'eval-attest-a1': inference provider nebius_tokenfactory; submission runs must use NVIDIA Nemotron on Nebius Token Factory and are labeled separately.

Sealed and adversarial suites run one child process per test under a supervisor that never imports candidate code and is the first step of its branch; two verifier canaries detect blanket result forgery. A candidate can still forge its own result from inside a child after the nonce was read if it spares the canaries (the mutation gate and held-out tests are the structural detectors).

The repository's own suite and the held-out suite run after the sealed verification in their own branches. They are bound through the same supervisor only for unittest repositories whose tests are statically discoverable; otherwise they are parsed from console output and the gate is labelled evidence_class 'stdout'.

Model-written sealed and adversarial tests can be wrong; their failures block VERIFIED. An independent arbiter then classifies each failure (implementation bug, test defect or contract dispute) and, for pure test defects, corrects and re-verifies them (must pass on the candidate and still fail on the base). Arbitration is advisory by default and never clears an implementation bug or a contract dispute; it changes the verdict only in explicit apply mode.
Grounding runs only when the specification names external references; sources are cited, not verified for correctness.
Sandbox CPU/RAM quota controls were not found in the current public REST API; per operation only max_layer_bytes, a timeout and the networking flag are set.
Sandbox raw 'cost' diagnostics are not USD; Codex gateway usage is ChatGPT allowance, not a Nebius charge; Nebius USD is computed from the public price table, not an invoice.
Each run retains one checkpoint image on the service; no image-delete control was found in the current public REST API.
